title: A meal with a journey
hook: The biggest reward is not always the largest net gain.

knows: Animals can act and respond to conditions.
doesNotKnow: In a toy foraging model, patch A gives 5 energy units and costs 1 to reach; B gives 8 and costs 6. Which has the larger net energy?

misconception: One observed behavior always supports a broad or causal conclusion.
objective: In a toy foraging model, patch A gives 5 energy units and costs 1 to reach; B gives 8 and costs 6. Which has the larger net energy?

claims.text: In a toy foraging model, patch A gives 5 energy units and costs 1 to reach; B gives 8 and costs 6. Which has the larger net energy? Patch A nets 5 − 1 = 4 energy units. Patch B nets 8 − 6 = 2, even though B offers more food. This toy counts only the stated energy benefit and travel cost; real foragers face other costs and uncertainty.
claims.source: Stipulated toy observations; not observed animal data. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
A new toy patch gives 9 energy units and costs 3 to reach. What is its net energy? 9 units of food minus 3 travel units gives a net of 6.
